title: Shared sanitizer applied to journal path leaves can rewrite stored paths and mislabel crash recovery
description: Since commit 4adeac3 storage::codec::scrub_value runs the shared sanitizer (removarr_domain::redact::sanitize) on every string leaf of journal intent target and observed values and of step final_state. A path leaf containing a whitespace-delimited word such as Basic, Bearer or Digest (the next word is replaced), a standalone sensitive key with an empty value such as Key: or Pass: (the rest of the line is replaced), a sensitive key=value pair after a comma or semicolon, or /announce or :// (the word becomes [url]) is stored in mangled form. The mangled string is still a valid path, so deserialization succeeds. If the process crashes between the intent row and the result row of a file or tree removal, recovery stats the mangled path, finds nothing and reports the step as Mutated although the file was never deleted. Effect: the interrupted action is labelled ExecutedUnverified and the torrent gets an extra recheck instead of being reported as interrupted. No file, torrent or ARR mutation follows and recovery never re-issues commands. Most of the class existed in the old scrubber (Basic or Bearer, Key= or Key: rewritten as Key=[redacted], ://); new in 4adeac3 are Digest, /announce, many more key names, comma, semicolon and ampersand segmentation, and the rest-of-line rule. For a tree removal only the tree root directory path is a rewritten value; file names inside the snapshot are JSON object keys and are not scrubbed.
root_cause: Free-text credential redaction is applied to path-typed JSON leaves that recovery later parses back as authoritative paths and signatures.
intended_behavior: Persisted journal targets must round-trip exactly so recovery can compare them with the disk; redaction should apply to messages and reasons, not to path fields (or recovery must fail closed when a stored target was altered).

trace.description: Intent target and observed are passed through scrub_value before insertion (final_state at line 64).
Every string leaf, including RelPath strings, goes through scrub, which now calls the shared sanitizer.
Bearer, Basic and Digest redact the next word; an empty-value sensitive key redacts the rest of the line (line 83).
A stat of the mangled path gives Ok(None), mapped to Executed::Mutated.

evidence.description: scrub is now a thin call to removarr_domain::redact::sanitize.
For FsRemoveTree a mangled tree root directory path (snapshot.dir.rel) makes all_gone true and yields Mutated; names of entries inside the snapshot are map keys and are not scrubbed.
sanitize tests each whitespace-delimited word; a path word that is exactly a trigger word, or a keyed word, matches.

conditions.description: The process must crash between the intent row and the result row of a removal step.
The file path (or the tree root directory path) must contain a stand-alone trigger word such as Digest, Basic or Key:, or contain /announce, ://, or a sensitive key=value after a comma.

execution.attacker_perspective: A torrent or release provider who chooses file or folder names that end up in an approved deletion plan.
instructions: In an isolated fixture, record a removal intent for a target whose path contains the payload word.
Read the stored target back and compare it with the original.
Simulate a crash before the result row and run recovery with the file still present.
execution.observed_result: Source trace only: the stored path differs from the original, recovery sees no file and returns Mutated for an unchanged file. Not executed.

remediation.strategy: Do not sanitize path-typed leaves of target and observed (sanitize reason and message fields only), or make observe_fs_intent return Unobservable when the scrubbed target differs from the original. Add a round-trip regression test with names containing Digest, Key: and /announce.

likelihood.reason: Needs a crash inside a narrow window and an unusual release name.

impact.reason: Mislabelled interrupted action plus an extra qBittorrent recheck; no wrong deletion or re-execution.

confidence.reason: Source-traced and independently verified by a fresh verifier; not executed because sandbox controls are not enforceable here.

title: Login limiter collapses to one shared bucket behind a reverse proxy when trusted_proxies is unset (visibility added, exposure unchanged)
description: Carried from run-1. Commit 4adeac3 adds a one-time warning event forwarded_header_untrusted_peer and documentation, and a test that shows the shared bucket, the per-IP window of 20, expiry after 15 minutes and separation once the proxy network is trusted. The limits and the rule that X-Forwarded-For is ignored from an untrusted peer are unchanged, so with an empty trusted_proxies behind a proxy all clients still share one bucket and 5 failed logins with the operator username per window block the operator login (reserve runs before verification). Existing sessions are unaffected. The behavior is intended fail-closed design; exposure depends on deployment. The warning can be consumed by any unauthenticated POST /login that carries an X-Forwarded-For header (it fires before the origin and CSRF checks), so it is a hint, not a guarantee.
claimed_root_cause: Default empty trusted_proxies plus per-peer-IP limiter keys; deployment must set REMOVARR_TRUSTED_PROXIES behind a proxy.

trace.description: Peer address is used unless the peer is a trusted proxy.
New once-only warning when X-Forwarded-For arrives from an untrusted peer; logs only the peer address.
Refuses when the per-IP or per-IP-and-username window is full, before password verification.

evidence.description: New test: shared bucket, 429 with Retry-After, expiry, and trusted 172.18.0.0/16 separating clients (read, not executed).
Hardening item 4 now explains the shared bucket and the log event.

blockers: Whether the operator runs a reverse proxy in front of the container.
Peer address Docker presents (bridge gateway or proxy).
Whether a proxy or WAF limit prevents an attacker sustaining the failed attempts.

validation_plan.local: Run the new auth_flow test in a skill-conformant sandbox (no network, empty environment, scratch-local target copy and limits) to confirm behavior; the test source already encodes the expected results.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner checks their own login_failed and login_succeeded log lines for client_ip equal to the proxy or gateway address and for the forwarded_header_untrusted_peer event; set trusted_proxies accordingly.
